newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: VENEZUELA CARBON ANODE PLANT HIT BY EXPLOSION.
newsitem.headline: VENEZUELA CARBON ANODE PLANT HIT BY EXPLOSION.

text.p: A carbon anode plant at Venezuela's state-owned aluminum smelter Venalum will be shut down for two days after being damaged by an explosion, Venalum said.
Despite Wednesday's blast, the smelter has 7,000 anodes in store which would be enough to maintain aluminum production levels until the plant was repaired, Venalum said in a release.
Venalum, Venezuela's largest aluminum smelter, produced about 445,000 tonnes of primary aluminum in 1996.
The company said the explosion was caused by a concentration of gases.
Venalum, smelter Alcasa, carbon anode producer Carbonorca and bauxite producer Bauxilum, are set to be privatized this year with a controlling 70 percent interest sold to an international consortium.
